name: Tonsillectomy
summary: How expats navigate tonsillectomy decisions in Singapore for recurring tonsillitis or sleep-disordered breathing — ENT counselling, recovery diet in hawker culture, and school/work downtime.
body:
Tonsillectomy is considered after repeated bacterial tonsillitis, quinsy history, or obstructive sleep symptoms with large tonsils — especially in kids. ENT assessment pairs history with exam; sleep studies may enter the pathway when breathing pauses dominate.

## Decision factors
- Infection frequency and antibiotic courses per year
- Sleep snoring / apnoea overlap in children
- Bleeding risk counselling and age considerations
- Alternatives when watchful waiting still makes sense
- Same-week emergency for peritonsillar abscess (not elective booking)

Adults recover slower than marketing implies; plan soft foods and time off.

## Recovery practicalities
Humidity and spicy hawker defaults clash with raw surgical throats — stock porridge, yoghurt, and ice ahead. Ask about return-to-school/sports and when flying is allowed. Pain peaks can surprise parents at day 5–7.

## How to choose
Prefer ENTs who quantify infection criteria and bleeding protocols, not only “take them out.” Confirm hospital after-hours contacts. Insurance often covers medically indicated tonsillectomy with pre-auth — cosmetic snore marketing is different.

## Practical tip
Set calendar reminders for antibiotic/analgesic timing after discharge. Keep the A&E plan for secondary bleeding — rare but time-critical.
